title: Paul's Journey to Jerusalem, Farewell to the Ephesian Elders

questions.question: At Troas during the weekly meeting, Paul spoke until midnight. A young man named Eutychus was sitting in a window and sank into a deep sleep. What happened?
options: He fell from the third story and was taken up dead; Paul embraced him and his life returned
He fell into a deep trance and prophesied for several hours
He fell from his chair and was healed by Paul immediately
He fell asleep and the prayer of the church restored him
questions.correctAnswer: He fell from the third story and was taken up dead; Paul embraced him and his life returned
questions.explanation: Acts 20:9-10 (ESV): "And a young man named Eutychus, sitting at the window, sank into a deep sleep... and fell down from the third story and was taken up dead. But Paul went down and bent over him, and taking him in his arms, said, 'Do not be alarmed, for his life is in him.'"

questions.question: Paul was hastening to be in Jerusalem by the Day of Pentecost. He bypassed Ephesus but called the Ephesian elders to meet him where?
options: Miletus
Troas
Corinth
Philippi
questions.explanation: Acts 20:17 (ESV): "Now from Miletus he sent to Ephesus and called the elders of the church to come to him."

questions.question: In his farewell address, Paul reminded the elders he had served among them with all humility and tears and what else?
options: Trials that came upon him through the plots of the Jews
Long hours of prayer and fasting on their behalf
Great physical hardships in the heat of Asia
Many conflicts with false teachers in the region
questions.correctAnswer: Trials that came upon him through the plots of the Jews
questions.explanation: Acts 20:19 (ESV): "serving the Lord with all humility and with tears and with trials that happened to me through the plots of the Jews;"

questions.question: Paul declared he had not shrunk from declaring anything that was profitable and had taught them publicly and from house to house, testifying about what two things?
options: Repentance toward God and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ
The kingdom of God and the resurrection of the dead
The forgiveness of sins and the gift of the Holy Spirit
Judgment to come and grace available through Christ Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: Repentance toward God and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: Acts 20:21 (ESV): "testifying both to Jews and to Greeks of repentance toward God and of faith in our Lord Jesus Christ."

questions.question: Paul said the Holy Spirit testified: "imprisonment and afflictions await me" in Jerusalem. But what was his response to this?
options: "But I do not account my life of any value nor as precious to myself, if only I may finish my course and the ministry I received from the Lord Jesus."
"I trust God to deliver me from all that awaits."
"The grace of God is sufficient for whatever lies ahead."
"I have already surrendered my life to God's purposes."
questions.correctAnswer: "But I do not account my life of any value nor as precious to myself, if only I may finish my course and the ministry I received from the Lord Jesus."
questions.explanation: Acts 20:24 (ESV): "But I do not account my life of any value nor as precious to myself, if only I may finish my course and the ministry that I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify to the gospel of the grace of God."

questions.question: Paul warned that after his departure, fierce wolves would come in, not sparing the flock. What other danger would arise from within?
options: Men speaking twisted things, to draw away the disciples after them
False prophets claiming new revelations beyond the apostles' teaching
Teachers denying the resurrection and promoting Greek philosophy
Leaders who would sell the church's property for personal gain
questions.correctAnswer: Men speaking twisted things, to draw away the disciples after them
questions.explanation: Acts 20:30 (ESV): "and from among your own selves will arise men speaking twisted things, to draw away the disciples after them."

questions.question: Paul commended the Ephesian elders to God and to "the word of his grace, which is able to build you up and to give you the inheritance among all those who are..."?
options: "sanctified."
"saved."
"beloved."
"chosen."
questions.explanation: Acts 20:32 (ESV): "And now I commend you to God and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up and to give you the inheritance among all those who are sanctified."

questions.question: Paul reminded the elders that he had coveted no one's silver or gold or clothing. He quoted a saying of the Lord Jesus that is not recorded in the four Gospels. What did it say?
options: "It is more blessed to give than to receive."
"The laborer is worthy of his hire."
"Whoever saves his life will lose it."
"Where your treasure is there your heart will be also."
questions.correctAnswer: "It is more blessed to give than to receive."
questions.explanation: Acts 20:35 (ESV): "In all things I have shown you that by working hard in this way we must help the weak and remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he himself said, 'It is more blessed to give than to receive.'"

questions.question: Paul called the Ephesian elders to be shepherds of the church. What did he say the Holy Spirit had made them?
options: Overseers, to care for the church of God which he obtained with his own blood
Elders and servants of the flock placed under their care
Guardians appointed by God to preserve the apostolic teaching
Teachers commissioned to train the next generation of leaders
questions.correctAnswer: Overseers, to care for the church of God which he obtained with his own blood
questions.explanation: Acts 20:28 (ESV): "Pay careful attention to yourselves and to all the flock, in which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers, to care for the church of God, which he obtained with his own blood."

questions.question: When Paul finished speaking and prayed with all the elders, what happened?
options: There was much weeping on all sides; they embraced Paul and kissed him, being sorrowful because he said they would not see his face again
They fell to their knees and prayed for three hours together
The elders gave Paul gifts and supplies for his journey to Jerusalem
They sang a hymn of praise before sending him off with joy
questions.correctAnswer: There was much weeping on all sides; they embraced Paul and kissed him, being sorrowful because he said they would not see his face again
questions.explanation: Acts 20:37-38 (ESV): "And there was much weeping on the part of all; they embraced Paul and kissed him, being sorrowful most of all because of the word he had spoken, that they would not see his face again."

questions.question: Paul told the elders he was innocent of the blood of all of them. Why?
options: Because he did not shrink from declaring to them the whole counsel of God
Because he had prayed for them daily and warned them constantly
Because he had appointed elders to continue his ministry
Because he had written down all his teaching for them to keep
questions.correctAnswer: Because he did not shrink from declaring to them the whole counsel of God
questions.explanation: Acts 20:26-27 (ESV): "Therefore I testify to you this day that I am innocent of the blood of all, for I did not shrink from declaring to you the whole counsel of God."

questions.question: Where did Paul go after leaving Troas and before arriving at Miletus?
options: Through Assos, Mitylene, Chios, Samos — a coastal route
Directly by sea from Troas to Miletus
Through Macedonia and down through Achaia
Via Ephesus but he did not enter the city
questions.correctAnswer: Through Assos, Mitylene, Chios, Samos — a coastal route
questions.explanation: Acts 20:13-15 (ESV): "But going ahead to the ship, we set sail for Assos, intending to take Paul aboard there... And from there we set sail and arrived the following day opposite Chios; the next day we touched at Samos; and the day after that we came to Miletus."

questions.question: While in Troas after Eutychus was raised, Paul continued talking how long?
options: Until daybreak
Until midnight
Until the third hour
Until the crowd dispersed
questions.explanation: Acts 20:11 (ESV): "And when Paul had gone up and had broken bread and eaten, he conversed with them a long while, until daybreak, and so departed."

questions.question: Paul said he had worked with his own hands to supply his needs and the needs of his companions. This was to support what principle?
options: That hard work honors God and enables us to help the weak
That ministers should never charge for the gospel they preach
That all believers should support themselves and not rely on others
That Paul was entitled to support but chose not to take it
questions.correctAnswer: That hard work honors God and enables us to help the weak
questions.explanation: Acts 20:34-35 (ESV): "You yourselves know that these hands ministered to my necessities and to those who were with me. In all things I have shown you that by working hard in this way we must help the weak..."

questions.question: Paul said he "did not account his life of any value" as long as he could finish his ministry. What specific ministry did he receive from the Lord Jesus?
options: "to testify to the gospel of the grace of God"
"to preach to the Gentiles and their kings"
"to plant churches from Jerusalem to Illyricum"
"to write letters that would guide the church forever"
questions.correctAnswer: "to testify to the gospel of the grace of God"
questions.explanation: Acts 20:24 (ESV): "if only I may finish my course and the ministry that I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify to the gospel of the grace of God."

key_verse_text: "But I do not account my life of any value nor as precious to myself, if only I may finish my course and the ministry that I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify to the gospel of the grace of God."
